metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after price spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 2–5% for high-velocity upward moves.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >80), model tends to overshoot and fail to correct — apply a “cool-down” rule: cap forecast at 10% below peak for 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence — reduce forecast volatility by 30–50% and anchor to recent 7-day moving average.
- Mean reversion bias is strong in late horizon (days 20–30) — if forecast is >10% above recent 14-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after spike (e.g., 85→75), model often fails to anticipate — add a “reversal buffer”: if 3 consecutive days >85, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3 days.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are prone to “tail risk” overestimation — apply a 10–15% downward adjustment if true outcome shows >10% volatility in last 5 days.
